lessons.title: Stack vs Heap Allocation Rules
lessons.description: Primitive values live on the stack; objects live on the heap. Understanding allocation helps prevent memory issues.

sections.heading: Stack vs Heap
list: Stack — fixed-size, fast, stores primitives and references
Heap — dynamic-size, stores objects, arrays and functions
Stack allocation is automatic and very fast
Heap allocation requires garbage collection to free memory

codeExamples.heading: Allocation in action
explanation: Primitives are copied by value — changing one doesn't affect the other.
Objects are referenced — both variables point to the same heap object.
Stack is fast but limited; heap is flexible but needs garbage collection.
References on the stack point to objects on the heap.

practice.task: Create a primitive and an object. Copy both to new variables. Modify the originals and explain why the primitive copy is unaffected but the object copy is.
hints: Primitives: let a = 5; let b = a; a = 10; — b is still 5.
Objects: let o1 = {x:1}; let o2 = o1; o1.x = 2; — o2.x is 2.
Stack vs heap explains the difference.

keyTakeaways: Primitives live on the stack and are copied by value.
Objects live on the heap and are accessed by reference.
Stack allocation is automatic and fast; heap needs garbage collection.
Understanding this prevents subtle bugs with object mutations.
lessons.challenge: Draw a memory diagram showing stack and heap allocation for a code snippet with variables, objects and arrays.

lessons.title: Mark-and-Sweep Garbage Collection Algorithm
lessons.description: V8's garbage collector frees memory by marking reachable objects and sweeping unreachable ones.

sections.heading: How mark-and-sweep works
list: Mark phase — starts from root objects (global, call stack) and marks all reachable objects
Runs automatically — you don't call it manually
Objects with zero references are candidates for collection

codeExamples.heading: Reachability and garbage collection
explanation: Objects reachable from roots (global, active functions) survive collection.
obj2 is not returned and goes out of scope — it becomes unreachable.
Setting result = null breaks the reference — obj1 is now collectable.
Garbage collection runs automatically when memory pressure is detected.

practice.task: Create a function that allocates many objects and returns only one. Use Chrome DevTools Memory profiler to observe garbage collection.
hints: Create 1000 objects in a loop, return only the last one.
Open DevTools → Memory → take a heap snapshot.
Observe the object count before and after garbage collection.

keyTakeaways: Mark-and-sweep marks reachable objects and frees unreachable ones.
Objects become eligible for collection when no references point to them.
Setting variables to null breaks references and allows collection.
Garbage collection runs automatically — you don't call it manually.
lessons.challenge: Profile a web application's memory usage over time using Chrome DevTools Memory tab.

lessons.title: Generational GC: Scavenger (Young) vs Mark-Compact (Old)
lessons.description: V8 uses generational garbage collection — different strategies for young and old objects.

sections.heading: Generational collection
list: Young generation (Scavenger) — short-lived objects collected frequently and quickly
Old generation (Mark-Compact) — long-lived objects collected less frequently
Most objects die young — the Scavenger handles them efficiently
Objects that survive multiple Scavenger cycles are promoted to the old generation

codeExamples.heading: Generational collection in practice
explanation: Short-lived objects in loops are collected quickly by the Scavenger.
Long-lived objects like caches are promoted to the old generation.
The Scavenger runs frequently and is very fast.
Mark-Compact runs less frequently but handles larger memory spaces.

practice.task: Explain why V8 uses generational collection instead of collecting all objects at once.
hints: Most objects die young — collecting them is cheap.
Long-lived objects need different collection strategies.
Separating them optimizes for both cases.

keyTakeaways: V8 separates objects into young and old generations.
The Scavenger quickly collects short-lived objects.
Mark-Compact handles long-lived objects less frequently.
Objects are promoted from young to old after surviving multiple collections.
lessons.challenge: Use Chrome DevTools to observe generational garbage collection in real time during a page interaction.
